vars.prTitle: Account sessions: compute expiration with SessionExpirationUtils
vars.prBody: The account console computed the session "expires" value by hand from ssoSessionMaxLifespan / ssoSessionMaxLifespanRememberMe, which ignores realm defaults when the lifespan is unset, the max() semantics for remember-me and offline sessions. Use the shared SessionExpirationUtils helper that the session validity checks already use.
vars.goldenComments: [{"comment": "SessionResource.createSessionRepresentation now calls SessionExpirationUtils.calculateUserSessionMaxLifespanTimestamp(offline, rememberMe, s.getStarted(), realm), but that helper works in milliseconds: it adds TimeUnit.SECONDS.toMillis(lifespan) to the 'created' argument and returns an epoch-millis timestamp (see AuthenticationManager.isSessionValid, which passes TimeUnit.SECONDS.toMillis(userSession.getStarted()) and compares with Time.currentTimeMillis()). Passing getStarted() in seconds and casting to int yields started + lifespan*1000, i.e. an expiration ~1000x the lifespan in the future (10h becomes ~416 days); with a long remember-me lifespan (e.g. 30 days) the sum exceeds Integer.MAX_VALUE and the (int) cast produces a negative value. It also returns -1 for offline sessions without max lifespan. The account REST API / console shows wrong expiry times.", "severity": "High"}]
